volantis: Volantis is the oldest and greatest of the Nine Free Cities, situated at the expansive mouth of the Rhoyne, revered as the first daughter of Old Valyria and mistress of the Summer Sea. The city is bisected by the broad waters of the Rhoyne into eastern and western halves—the eastern enclave shielded by the immense Black Walls, reserved exclusively for the patrician Old Blood who can trace their lineage to Valyria's dragonlords, and the western sector inhabited by sellswords, craftsmen, and commoners, connected only by the monumental Long Bridge. Volantene civic politics are fiercely contested between the militant Tiger party, who yearn for imperial conquest, and the mercantile Elephant faction, who prioritize maritime trade and commercial profits. The grand Red Temple wields immense ideological authority, where High Priestess Kinvara openly proclaims Daenerys Targaryen as the promised savior, bringing not merely divine prophecies but zealous legions of the Fiery Hand to her cause. Clinging proudly to ancient Valyrian architecture and chattel slavery, Volantis watches the shifting tides of the world with imperious detachment, ready to crush any threat to its ancient dominion.
sturgia: The Iron Islands comprise a harsh archipelago consisting of Pyke, Great Wyk, Old Wyk, Harlaw, and Saltcliffe, anchored in Ironman's Bay off the rugged western coast of Westeros. The soil is bleak and stony, rich in iron and lead but incapable of feeding its populace through agriculture alone. Since the Dawn Age, the ironborn have sustained themselves by the reaver's craft, living by the axe, the oar, and the uncompromising decree that they do not sow. Their seat of sovereignty is Pyke, the ancient castle of House Greyjoy built upon sea stacks lashed by roaring breakers. Following the death of King Robert, Balon Greyjoy has crowned himself King of the Iron Islands once more. His first rebellion was crushed in blood years ago, with his last surviving son Theon taken to Winterfell as a hostage—an exile that stoked Balon's bitter hatred for the mainland green-landers. Governed not by Andal primogeniture but by the martial code that every captain is a king upon his own quarterdeck, ironborn society is consecrated by the Drowned God, whose priests perform ritual drownings to seal rebirth. Balon's fierce daughter Asha commands swift longships and advocates conquering fertile northern coastlands rather than barren raids, while his exiled brother Euron represents a far darker menace from the smoking ruins of Valyria. When mustered, the Iron Fleet commands peerless mastery over the waves, unmatched in amphibious raids and boarding actions, poised to strike deep into the bleeding wounds of Westeros.
riverlands: Centered upon the sandstone fortress of Riverrun, the Riverlands embrace the rich plains of the Trident basin, the hamlets along the Green Fork, the agricultural hearthlands of the Red Fork, and the vital artery of the Kingsroad. The realm possesses no natural boundaries to deter invaders—it is devoid of mountain bulwarks to the south, protective bogs to the north, sea barriers to the west, or colossal walls to the east. The Red, Green, and Blue Forks grant lush fertility and commerce, yet divide the domain into isolated fragments. This geographic crossroads dictates its tragic history: every war between north and south marches across its soil, and every host relies on riverland grain, ferries, and bridges. Though ruled in name by House Tully, feudal power is fractured among contentious bannermen—the bitter feud between Blackwood and Bracken stretches back millennia, House Mallister guards the western coast against ironborn longships, and House Vance controls the southern passes to the Vale. With Lord Hoster Tully ailing, Riverrun falls to his earnest son Edmure, whose chivalric heart struggles against military realities. The Riverlands have become the bloody crucible of the War of the Five Kings; Lord Tywin's vanguard under Gregor Clegane has put crops and holds to the torch, turning fertile fields into smoking desolation. Though Robb Stark's northern victories have temporarily lifted the siege of Riverrun, the ruthless grinding of armies threatens to reduce the realm to an impoverished ash heap.
lys: Known throughout Essos as Lys the Lovely, this Free City rises from rocky islands surrounded by tempestuous turquoise waters in the Summer Sea. Wealthy beyond measure, Lys is built entirely upon commercial navigation, opulent pleasure houses, and an extensive slave market, famed across the known world for cultivating exquisite bedslaves and brewing untraceable poisons—most notorious among them the tears of Lys and the Strangler. Civic affairs are directed by a council of magisters selected from the wealthiest merchant dynasties, who conduct statecraft not on the field of honor, but in perfumed salons through bribes, assassination, and proxy hirelings. The sleek trading galleys of Lys dominate maritime commerce between the Narrow Sea and the Stepstones. Maintaining formal neutrality in the War of the Five Kings, Lysian financiers, sellsword brokers, and assassins nevertheless circle the chaos of Westeros, poised to harvest colossal fortunes from continental ruin.
myr: Situated along the western shores of Essos upon the calm waters of the Sea of Myr, the Free City of Myr is celebrated as a metropolis of peerless artisan guilds and thriving manufactories. Its craftsmen produce the world's finest ground lenses and far-eyes cherished at the Citadel of Oldtown, alongside exquisite tapestries, delicate lace, and tinted glass panes. Myrish crossbowmen command immense renown throughout the sellsword markets, equipped with rapid repeating mechanisms of deadly precision. The city is governed by an oligarchy of merchant magisters chosen from prominent trading houses. While preserving an official posture of neutrality in the War of the Five Kings, Myr serves as a vital armory and supplier, funneling masterwork weapons, artisan wares, and mercenary contracts into the warring factions of the Seven Kingdoms.
battania: Ruling from the ancient gray fastness of Winterfell, the realm of the North encompasses the vast peninsula stretching from the impenetrable bogs of the Neck and the ruins of Moat Cailin in the south to the monolithic ice of the Wall in the north. Covering nearly forty percent of Westeros, the North is a land of brooding pine forests, windswept barrows, and sparse settlements clustered around Winterfell, the bustling port of White Harbor, and solitary mountain clanholds. Contact relies upon the Kingsroad and coastal anchorages, both easily smothered by winter blizzards. For eight thousand years, House Stark has governed this harsh frontier. Following the unjust beheading of Lord Eddard Stark in King's Landing, his fifteen-year-old heir Robb Stark summoned the northern bannermen and marched south, proclaimed King in the North by sword and oath. His host unites varied ambitions: House Manderly funds the campaign through White Harbor's sea trade; House Umber contributes ferocious shock infantry; House Karstark brings grim cavalry demanding blood for blood; House Bolton provides disciplined battalions under Lord Roose's cold eye; and House Reed guards the secret paths of the Neck. Reared in frost and stone, northern infantry display unbreakable stamina in mud and snow. Having shattered the Lannisters at the Whispering Wood and captured Jaime Lannister, the Young Wolf has proven his tactical brilliance, yet securing long-term victory requires iron resolve to hold his fragile coalition together.
yiti: Composed of political exiles and wandering envoys from the far east, this community represents the Golden Empire of Yi Ti—the vast and ancient civilization situated at the farthest edge of the known world. In their homeland, the God-Emperors preside over sprawling jade metropolises, supported by a colossal bureaucratic mandarin system and veteran standing armies. YiTish silks, delicate porcelain, and rare saffron spices command princely sums across the bazaars of Pentos and Volantis. While detached from the dynastic bloodletting of the Seven Kingdoms, these eastern outcasts preserve their ancestral customs, philosophical doctrines, and merchant leagues, viewing the War of the Five Kings as the fleeting squabble of distant barbarians.
aserai: Commanded from the sand-swept spires of Sunspear, Dorne rules the southernmost peninsula of Westeros, walled off from the north by the red mountain peaks of the Prince's Pass and the Boneway, and bordered by the sun-baked waters of the Greenblood delta and the Summer Sea. The blistering desert and treacherous canyons render large-scale invasion nearly impossible; historically, even Aegon the Conqueror's dragons failed to break the Dornish spirit. Sustained by river oases, coastal fisheries, and secluded wells, Dorne's primary defender is its burning sun and desiccating sands. Infused with Rhoynish traditions brought by Queen Nymeria, Dorne honors equal inheritance for women and embraces natural-born children without prejudice, retaining the royal title of Prince of Dorne. Prince Doran Martell has governed for over two decades, cloaking his acute strategic genius beneath gout and a wheelchair in the Water Gardens. His brother, Prince Oberyn—the Red Viper—is a lethal duelist and master of venom who roams the courts of Essos and King's Landing as Doran's mailed fist. Dornish martial doctrine favors elusive sand steeds, nimble lancers, and javelin skirmishers, formidable in desert ambushes. Though Doran maintains rigid neutrality in the War of the Five Kings, Dorne's silence is neither cowardice nor apathy: the brutal murder of Princess Elia and her children during the sack of King's Landing remains an unavenged debt of blood that will be paid in full.
summer: Scattered across the sapphire expanse of the Summer Sea south of Westeros, the Summer Isles comprise more than fifty lush, emerald islands. Celebrated for their ebony skin, vibrant feather cloaks, and master craftsmanship, the Summer Islanders are unrivaled mariners and peerless archers. Their colossal swan-ships dominate ocean trade lanes, and their tall bows carved from goldenheart wood outrange any longbow in Westeros. Governed in peace by princes chosen under the guidance of the Goldenheart Council, the islands regard warfare with abhorrence, resolving disputes through ritual non-lethal duels. In the turmoil of the War of the Five Kings, the Summer Isles maintain absolute neutrality, offering sanctuary, oceanic navigation, and precious trade to all who respect their shores.
nightswatch: Stretching one hundred leagues across the frozen neck of northern Westeros, the Wall stands as a colossal bulwark of ice, gravel, and spellcraft, soaring over seven hundred feet above the haunted forest. Raised eight thousand years ago after the Long Night, the ancient brotherhood of the Night's Watch once garrisoned nineteen great fortresses with ten thousand sworn brothers. Today, only Castle Black, the Shadow Tower, and Eastwatch-by-the-Sea remain manned, their muster dwindled to less than a thousand men. Divided into rangers who patrol the wilderness, builders who tend the ice, and stewards who provision the halls, the black brothers forswear lands, titles, and lineage to defend the realms of men. Lord Commander Jeor Mormont has led two hundred elite rangers north on the Great Ranging to investigate missing patrols and wildling gatherings, leaving Castle Black in the hands of castellan Bowen Marsh. Young Jon Snow, newly appointed steward to the Lord Commander, rapidly discovers the grim realities of leadership. Starved of men and supplies from southern kingdoms deaf to its pleas, the Night's Watch faces an existential crisis: Mance Rayder's one hundred thousand wildlings march upon the Wall to breach the gates, while deep in the haunted darkness of the far north, the true ancient threat—the Others of legend—has awakened to extinguish the world of the living.
bravos: Sprawled across a secret labyrinth of lagoons and canals where the Narrow Sea meets the Shivering Sea, Braavos is the wealthiest and most formidable of the Free Cities. Founded in secret by escaped slaves fleeing Valyrian dragonlords, the city is ruled by the Sea Lord and guarded by the colossal bronze Titan standing astride the harbor entrance. Braavosi shipbuilders can assemble a complete war galley in a single day at the Arsenal, endowing the city with an invincible armada. Its citizens practice the deadly, elegant water dance with slender bravos' blades, while within its misty alleys stands the House of Black and White, ancestral seat of the Faceless Men. Most feared of all is the Iron Bank of Braavos, whose golden vaults finance kings and emperors across the known world. The Iron Bank's terrifying creed is inviolable: when a monarch defaults on his debt, the Bank funds his deadliest rival to seize the crown. Though outwardly neutral in the War of the Five Kings, the Iron Bank holds the financial destiny of the Iron Throne in its iron grip.
norvos: Perched upon terraced hills along the eastern bluffs of the River Noyne, Norvos is a solemn theocratic Free City known for its rich tapestries, thick woolens, and shipwright oak. The city is ruled by the mysterious Bearded Priests from their fortress temple, directing civic life according to sacred rites and ringing carillons from three holy bells—Noom, Narrah, and Nyfer. The city is split between the Upper City on high bluffs, where the priestly nobility resides, and the Lower City by the river docks, joined by the monumental Sinner's Steps where bears dance during festivals. The priesthood maintains an elite guard of tattooed slave-soldiers armed with formidable longaxes, whose unflinching discipline and absolute loyalty are revered across Essos. Maintaining an austere and disciplined order, Norvos watches continental affairs with calm detachment, preserving its mountain trade routes and temple peace.
empire_s: Operating across the historic slaving hubs of Astapor, Yunkai, and Meereen in Essos, the faction of House Targaryen is centered around the remarkable rise of Daenerys Targaryen. Having hatched three living dragons from Khal Drogo's funeral pyre, the young princess transformed from a penniless exile into an unstoppable conqueror. At Astapor, she purchased eight thousand Unsullied—the world's most disciplined eunuch infantry—and unleashed them to slaughter the Good Masters. Sweeping through Yunkai and taking Meereen, she abolished chattel slavery, establishing a revolutionary regime dedicated to human liberty. Advised by the exiled Westerosi knight Ser Jorah Mormont, the scribe Missandei, and the Unsullied commander Grey Worm, Daenerys has declared herself Queen of Meereen. Her dragons—Drogon, Rhaegal, and Viserion—grow more ferocious each month, serving as living avatars of Valyrian supremacy. Yet governing Meereen plunges her into bitter asymmetric warfare against the Sons of the Harpy and trade blockades by slave cities, forcing her to learn the agonizing art of statecraft before she can ever set sail to reclaim her ancestral throne in Westeros.
freefolk: The Free Folk inhabit the vast, untamed wilderness stretching beyond the Wall—from the tangled depths of the Haunted Forest to the jagged spires of the Frostfangs, along the icy Milkwater and the glacier-carved valleys of Thenn. Acknowledging no hereditary lords, land deeds, or southron kings, they call themselves the Free Folk and scorn the men of the Seven Kingdoms as kneelers. Divided into hundreds of feuding clans, they have been forged by bitter cold and ferocious survival into natural hunters and trackers. Wildling women fight and command alongside men, with spearwives proving every bit as lethal as their male kin. Driven by the resurrection of ancient terrors in the far north, Mance Rayder—a former ranger of the Night's Watch who abandoned his vows—has achieved the impossible: uniting over one hundred thousand wildlings, Thenns, cave-dwellers, Hornfoot tribesmen, and even woolly mammoths and giants into a single host. Mance's campaign is not born of a conqueror's vanity, but of desperate flight from the icy grip of the Others. His objective is to shatter the Wall and lead his people to sanctuary in the fertile lands of the south before the Long Night swallows them whole.
tyrosh: Perched upon an island at the northeastern fringe of the Stepstones, Tyrosh is an exuberant and wealthy Free City founded upon thriving artisan manufactories and maritime piracy. The discovery of rare sea snails yielding brilliant purple dye transformed Tyrosh into an opulent mercantile hub. Its armorers and silversmiths are renowned for crafting ornate gilded helmets shaped like fantastic beasts and birds, while its citizens are famous for flamboyant attire and extravagantly dyed, forked beards. Ruled by an Archon elected through a volatile mix of merchant patronage, bribes, and intimidation, Tyrosh maintains close ties to mercenary free companies across the Disputed Lands. Guarding the sea gates of the Narrow Sea, Tyrosh profits immensely from leasing sellsword bands and selling military equipment to the warring realms of Westeros.
valyrian: This faction represents the secretive Targaryen restoration enterprise centered upon Prince Aegon Targaryen—alleged son of Crown Prince Rhaegar Targaryen and Princess Elia of Martell. Rescued in infancy from the sack of King's Landing by Master of Whisperers Varys and Lord Jon Connington, the young prince was raised in hiding along the riverbanks of the Rhoyne as 'Young Griff.' Lord Jon Connington, the former Hand of the King exiled by the Mad King, serves as his sworn guardian, military mentor, and father figure. Backed by the immense fortune of Magister Illyrio of Pentos, Aegon has secured the sacred contract of the Golden Company—ten thousand veteran exiles and knights founded by Bittersteel, celebrated as the most formidable sellsword brotherhood in the known world, who have never broken a contract. With Westeros torn apart by the War of the Five Kings, this disciplined host readies its galleys in Essos, preparing to land upon the shores of Westeros and reclaim the Iron Throne under the red dragon banner.
vlandia: House Baratheon of King's Landing holds the ancestral capital of the Seven Kingdoms and the surrounding Crownlands, controlling the Blackwater basin, the Kingsroad arteries, and loyalist castles such as Rosby and Duskendale. Dominating the mouth of the Blackwater from atop three hills, King's Landing houses half a million souls within its stone walls, divided between the red spires of the Red Keep and the squalid alleys of Flea Bottom. The regime is defended by the two-thousand-strong City Watch—the Gold Cloaks—and the veteran western bannermen deployed by House Lannister. King Joffrey Baratheon sits upon the Iron Throne, but his court is poisoned by factional intrigue, corruption, and the terrifying reality of his incestuous birth from Queen Cersei and Jaime Lannister. From the fortress of Harrenhal, Lord Tywin Lannister directs total war with cold precision, spending Casterly Rock's gold to sustain the war effort while his daughter Cersei mismanages the Small Council. Heavily reliant on river and sea convoys for grain, King's Landing faces starvation and siege from Renly's vast army to the south, Stannis's armada to the east, and Robb Stark's victories in the west, turning the royal capital into a boiling kettle ready to explode.
lorath: Nestled upon an archipelago of bleak islands in the Shivering Sea, west of the Axe and north of the Andal coast, Lorath is the most isolated and austere of the Free Cities. Erected atop ancient subterranean labyrinths carved by a forgotten civilization, the city was once shaped by the ascetic faith of Boash, leaving an enduring cultural imprint of humility, quietude, and plain speaking. With little involvement in continental geopolitics, Lorath's economy centers upon rich marine harvests—salt cod, walrus ivory, seal skins, and whale oil shipped to distant markets. Governed by a quiet council of magisters, Lorath remains largely untouched by the War of the Five Kings, pursuing its oceanic trades in undisturbed peace.
skagosi: Lying across the tempestuous entrance of the Bay of Seals, the mountainous island of Skagos is nominally part of the North but operates completely outside the writ of Winterfell. Known in the Old Tongue as the 'Stoneborn,' the clans of Skagos have a fearsome reputation for savagery, cannibalism, and fierce independence, accompanied by legends of giant horned beasts resembling unicorns. Culturally closer to the Free Folk than the feudal lords of the south, the islanders worship the Old Gods through ancient, unyielding rites. Isolated by treacherous currents and granite reefs, Skagos remains a mysterious and untamed wilderness, utterly indifferent to the distant clash of southron kings.
pentos: Situated on the eastern coast of the Narrow Sea directly opposite King's Landing, the Free City of Pentos is a sprawling, wealthy metropolis of square brick towers and walled manors. Officially governed by a ceremonial Prince and a ruling council of merchant magisters, Pentos has historically served as a haven for exiles, sellswords, and political conspirators. Prominent among them is Magister Illyrio Mopatis, an immensely wealthy merchant prince who provided sanctuary to Viserys and Daenerys Targaryen, arranged her marriage to Khal Drogo, and covertly coordinates the invasion plans of Prince Aegon and the Golden Company. Outwardly maintaining peaceful neutrality, Pentos acts as the grand financial and strategic chessboard through which the destinies of both Essos and Westeros are quietly manipulated.
stormlands: Anchored upon the colossal, seaward-facing drum tower of Storm's End, the Stormlands encompass the rugged coastal plains and wooded highlands of southeastern Westeros. Bounded by the Crownlands to the north, Dorne to the south, the Reach to the west, and the tempestuous Narrow Sea to the east, the region is shaped by howling ocean gales and relentless rains. This harsh climate has bred a martial, proud, and uncompromising people whose knights are famed for their valor. Storm's End itself, built by the legendary Brandon the Builder with thick granite walls infused with ancient spells, has never fallen to siege or assault. Following King Robert's death, his charismatic younger brother Renly Baratheon declared himself King, rallying the fierce stormlords alongside the mighty hosts of the Reach. Yet his claim is contested by his dour elder brother Stannis, sundering the stormlords into a bitter family schism. Blessed with veteran marcher lords and fierce shock cavalry, the Stormlands command immense battlefield prowess, though their lands risk exhaustion should their royal claimant fail to secure a swift victory.
dragonstone: Rising like a jagged obsidian fang from the waters of Blackwater Bay, Dragonstone is the ancestral volcanic island fortress of House Targaryen, currently held by King Stannis Baratheon. Hewn by Valyrian sorcery and dragonflame, its towers and battlements are shaped into gargoyles and stone dragons that seem to breathe amid volcanic mists. Stannis, Robert's elder surviving brother, has claimed the Iron Throne by strict legal right, denouncing Joffrey as an incestuous bastard. Renowned for unbending justice and cold military discipline, Stannis lacks courtly charm but possesses indomitable willpower. His strength resides in the Royal Fleet of the Narrow Sea and sworn island lords like Velaryon and Celtigar, guided by his loyal advisor Ser Davos Seaworth—the Onion Knight. The arrival of Lady Melisandre, a shadowbinder and red priestess from Asshai, has transformed Dragonstone into the crucible of R'hllor's worship, proclaiming Stannis as Azor Ahai reborn. Though vastly outnumbered on land by Tywin and Renly, Stannis's formidable fleet, lawful cause, and supernatural counsel make Dragonstone a deadly contender in the struggle for the Seven Kingdoms.
empire_w: Reigning from the palatial rose towers of Highgarden, the Reach governs the most fertile and populous domain in Westeros, embracing the emerald valleys of the Mander basin, the bustling wharves of Oldtown, and the vineyard slopes of the Arbor. As the breadbasket of the Seven Kingdoms, the Reach supplies grain, cattle, fruit, and celebrated Arbor vintage wines to the entire continent. At Oldtown, the Citadel serves as the venerable center of scholarship and medicine where maesters forge their chains, while the Hightower guards the mouth of the Whispering Sound. Revering courtly romance, chivalric pageantry, and tournament tournaments, Highgarden fields the largest and best-equipped knightly host in the realm, exemplified by Ser Loras Tyrell, the Knight of Flowers. Nominal leadership rests with Lord Mace Tyrell, though true strategic acumen is exercised by his formidable mother, Lady Olenna—the Queen of Thorns. By wedding Lady Margaery to Renly Baratheon, Highgarden has formed the formidable Stag-and-Rose alliance, putting more than one hundred thousand soldiers into the field to march on the Iron Throne.
empire: Perched atop the sheer granite heights of the Giant's Lance, the Vale of Arryn is ruled from the Eyrie, an impregnable palace of white towers overlooking fertile valleys stretching eastward to the Narrow Sea. Entrance to the realm is barred by the Bloody Gate—a narrow mountain chasm guarded by battlements where every attacking army in history has been shattered. The Vale is a self-sufficient haven of wheat fields, swift rivers, and prosperous ports such as Gulltown. Following Lord Jon Arryn's suspicious death, his widow Lady Lysa retreated to the Eyrie with her sickly son Robert, locking the mountain passes and declaring absolute neutrality in the War of the Five Kings. Though proud bannermen like House Royce yearn to ride to the aid of their northern kin, Lysa's paranoia keeps the peerless Knights of the Vale locked within their borders. Looming in the background is Petyr Baelish, whose subtle machinations seek to turn the untouched military host of the Vale into the ultimate weapon to advance his personal ambition.
qohor: Built along the banks of the River Qhoyne at the edge of the immense, untamed Forest of Qohor, this Free City is renowned throughout the world as the City of Sorcerers. Its skilled armorers possess the secret, lost arts of infusing vibrant colors into steel and reforging Valyrian steel blades with dark spells. Qohorik society is centered upon the worship of the Black Goat, a bloodthirsty deity propitiated by veiled priests through animal and human sacrifices. Following the famous historical defense where three thousand Unsullied shattered twenty-five thousand Dothraki horselords outside its gates, Qohor employs only Unsullied spearmen as its city guard. Operating as a pivotal inland crossroads between western Free Cities and the Dothraki Sea, Qohor guards its secret metallurgy and timber wealth with vigilant mystic discipline.
sarnor: This faction represents the proud remnants of the Kingdom of Sarnor, once the greatest civilization of eastern Essos inhabited by the tall, dark-eyed Sarnori people. In their golden age, Sarnori kings ruled over grand cities along the Sar River, taking the field in scythed chariots clad in iron and spider-silk armor. When the Doom of Valyria unleashed the Dothraki horselords, the divided Sarnori city-states were systematically sacked and put to the torch until only the coastal hold of Saath remained. Today, the surviving clans wander the edge of the grasslands, preserving their ancient lore, heroic epics, and chariot traditions amid the ruins of fallen palaces, dreaming of a day when the Century of Blood might finally be undone.
khuzait: Roaning across the colossal, rolling steppe known as the Dothraki Sea—which stretches from the Forest of Qohor eastward to the Bone Mountains—the Dothraki are a nomadic warrior culture whose entire existence revolves around horses. Divided into independent khalasars numbering tens of thousands of riders, each horde is governed by a paramount Khal whose absolute command rests solely upon martial prowess, plunder, and the respect of his bloodriders. Spurning armor as cowardly, Dothraki screamers ride bareback into battle armed with curved steel arakhs, bone daggers, and recurve horn bows, overwhelming adversaries with blistering speed and fluid cavalry maneuvers. Spurning stone cities and terrified of the sea, they maintain only the holy sanctuary of Vaes Dothrak in the shadow of the Mother of Mountains. Following the death of the mighty Khal Drogo and the birth of Daenerys Targaryen's dragons, the balance of power across the Great Grass Sea has fractured, opening an unpredictable era where the horselords may once again spill over the world.
